title: Ethiopian Spiced Beef Skewers
community: Ethiopian street food and restaurants — the charcoal beef skewer
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Beef Skewers — beef cubes marinated in berbere, kibbeh, garlic, and awaze, grilled over charcoal. Ethiopia's answer to the East African mishkaki — more elaborately spiced with the highland spice tradition.
longDesc: Ethiopian beef skewers are the street food of Addis Ababa's evening markets — the berbere and kibbeh marinade produces a skewer of extraordinary flavour that the charcoal caramelises magnificently.
steps: Mix marinade. Coat beef cubes. Marinate 1 hour minimum.
Grill over medium-high charcoal: 3—4 minutes per side.
The berbere should caramelise on the surface.
chefTips: The berbere caramelises beautifully — medium-high heat is perfect.
Awaze gives extra heat and depth.
commonMistakes: Over-cooking — berbere burns at very high heat.
cookingScience: Berbere contains sugars from the dried chillies and onion powder — these caramelise on the beef surface during grilling, creating the characteristic deep red-brown crust.
culturalNote: Ethiopian beef skewers are the food of Addis Ababa's evenings — the charcoal smoke and berbere fragrance drifting through the market streets.
